title: Rain at the market
text:
Every Saturday, Dewi helps Grandma at her fruit stall in the market. Grandma sells mangoes, bananas and bright orange papayas. Dewi's job is to put the fruit in neat rows and to smile at the shoppers.

One Saturday, dark clouds rolled over the hills. “It's going to rain soon,” said Grandma, looking up at the sky. “And we have nothing to cover the fruit.”

Dewi looked around the market. The fish seller had a big blue sheet. The flower seller had an old umbrella. Then Dewi spotted the pile of banana leaves at the back of the stall. They were wide and shiny, and Grandma used them to wrap the fruit for her shoppers.

“Grandma! We can use the leaves!” Dewi cried.

Together, they laid the banana leaves over the fruit, one on top of another, like the tiles on a roof. They finished just in time. The rain came pouring down. It drummed on the leaves, but the fruit underneath stayed dry.

When the sun came out again, the shoppers came back. “Your fruit looks so fresh!” said one lady, and she bought six mangoes.

Grandma gave Dewi a big hug. “What a clever idea,” she said. “Next Saturday, you can be the boss of the stall!”
